PullRequest.Title: agentHost: defer tools by default and allow-list runtime built-ins
PullRequest.Body:
Every tool the model can see costs input tokens on every request and is part of the prompt cache. Until now, a new Agent Host server tool was eager unless it opted into deferral, and a runtime built-in that shipped in a Copilot SDK bump was enabled for every session without anyone deciding to adopt it. This PR makes deferral the default and pins the eager set in tests.

### Changes
- **Server tools (Copilot only):** an unset `deferLoading` now maps to `defer: 'auto'`, so only an explicit `deferLoading: false` is eager. Claude and Codex keep their SDK defaults. Deferral still applies only when tool search is active.
- **Runtime built-ins:** the default `availableTools` is now `COPILOT_DEFAULT_AVAILABLE_TOOLS` (new `copilotBuiltinToolAllowlist.ts`), which is the adopted built-ins plus `custom:*` and `mcp:*`. A built-in that is not on the list stays off. `excludedTools` and per-model `availableTools` overrides behave as before.
- **What the allow-list contains:** only built-ins the current runtime registers for a host-enabled feature, plus their platform and setting variants: PowerShell, `local_shell`, `search_code_subagent`, tool search and `execution_subagent`. Names that are always excluded and names no runtime registers today are left out, so they cannot turn on silently in a later SDK.
- **Conditional built-ins left off until someone needs them:** these are runtime built-ins that only register under specific conditions. I checked when each appears in the runtime source. None is on the list, so each stays off for Agent Host Copilot sessions until it's reviewed and opted in.
  - `lsp`: when an LSP config exists in the project, the user's config or a plugin.
  - `fetch_copilot_cli_documentation`: in general-purpose subagents, which get the `cli-documentation` capability.
  - `catalog_search` and `catalog_select`: need the `DISCOVER_RESOURCES` flag, which the host never sets.
  - `str_replace_editor`: only for `oswe-*` models.

  The `vscode-ask` agent names `lsp` and the CLI documentation tool, but a custom agent's tool list only allows tools; it doesn't add them, so Ask is unaffected.
- **Recording:** the `copilotPromptsE2E` tool-list check is skipped while recording fixtures, like the prompt snapshot, because recording uses live model profiles and experiment assignments.
- **Guardrails:** tests now pin the eager server tools (`add_artifact_or_reference`), `NON_DEFERRED_CLIENT_TOOL_NAMES` (`runTests`) and the full model-facing tool list per model family in `copilotPromptsE2E`.
- **Allow-list drift test:** the new `providerIntegration/copilotBuiltinToolAllowlist.integrationTest.ts` runs the bundled SDK against the synthetic Copilot API stubs, for both tool profiles and the interactive, plan and autopilot modes. It fails when:
  - a registered built-in is neither allow-listed nor in `KNOWN_LEFT_OFF`, which catches new tools from an SDK bump;
  - an allow-listed name isn't registered and isn't in `NOT_EXERCISED`, which catches removed tools and typos in the list;
  - the default filter keeps anything other than the allow-listed built-ins.

  A rename fails in both directions.

  **Leaving a new tool off is the default fix, and renames keep their adoption.** The failure message prints each new built-in's description. The message, the code comments and the Agent Host instructions all say to check each new built-in for a rename first. A rename means an allow-listed tool is gone and a new one does the same job. For a rename, the fix replaces the old name in the allow-list and the expected tool list, adds the new name to the display mapping and regenerates the snapshots, so the capability stays on. Any other new built-in goes into `KNOWN_LEFT_OFF` with a reason, which keeps it off. They say never to adopt a new tool to make the test pass, so an agent asked to "fix the failing test" does the right thing in both cases. Adopting a tool is a decision for the tool budget owners. `.github/CODENOTIFY` notifies them about changes to the allow-list, the test (including `KNOWN_LEFT_OFF`) and the prompt baselines. It needs no account and runs in PR CI on macOS, Linux and Windows, in under a second. Feature- and experiment-gated built-ins (memory, canvases, image generation, the execution subagent, tool search) are deliberately out of scope and stay a manual check during SDK bumps.
- **Docs:**
  - Adds invariant I9 and a new §9 to `src/vs/platform/agentHost/AGENTS.md` covering when a tool earns an eager slot, a checklist for SDK bumps (including how to compare a runtime's built-ins with and without the allow-list), and where prompt text and reminders may go given their cache behavior.
  - Adds pointers in `prompts/AGENTS.md`, the E2E README and the Agent Host instructions file. The pointer is scoped to `src/vs/platform/agentHost/**` rather than the repo-wide `copilot-instructions.md`.
  - Adds CODENOTIFY entries for the allow-lists and baselines.

### Smoke test of the built-in allow-list
The replayed suites run without canvases, memory, autopilot or an account, so I checked the allow-list against the live runtime. I created signed-in SDK sessions with the host's config and feature flags, with canvases, memory (cloud and in-repo), image generation and tool search on, in interactive, plan and autopilot modes, across all 30 available models. I then compared `session.rpc.tools.getCurrentMetadata()` with `availableTools` unset and with the allow-list.

- The first version of the list dropped `vote_memory`, which Copilot Memory registers. It is now included.
- With the final list, the only built-ins removed are `semantic_code_search`, `run_dynamic_workflow` and `dynamic_workflows_manage`, which the host already excludes. Canvas, memory, plan mode, autopilot, image generation and every model family keep their full tool set.
- Not observed on this machine: the Windows shell family, and `tool_search_tool`, which does not appear in the metadata listing. Both are kept on the list.
- Compared against a live Copilot agent session (the agent that made these changes). Its runtime-built-in tools are all on the list. It also had `web_search` directly callable, so I sent one turn to let the runtime connect its own GitHub MCP server. The runtime reports `web_search` as coming from that server (`github-mcp-server`), so `mcp:*` keeps it and the allow-list does not drop it. §9 now documents this, and the probe step in the SDK-bump checklist now says to send one turn first.

The wire request is byte-identical for the replayed sessions: no `*.prompt.md` or traffic baseline changed.

### How to test
- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/providerIntegration/copilotBuiltinToolAllowlist.integrationTest.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/copilotPromptsE2E.integrationTest.ts`: 25 passing, no baselines regenerated.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts`: 158 passing.
- GitHub PR CI ran the allow-list test on Windows, Linux and macOS, and it passed on all three.
- `npm run typecheck-client` and `npm run eslint` on the changed files: clean.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or resume a Copilot Agent Host session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The launcher resolves existing BYOK, shell, plugin, prompt, and managed-settings inputs, constructs the fixed available-tools filter locally, then performs the existing SDK create/resume call. The changed allow-list construction is synchronous bounded array work on this path and adds no await or remote operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create or resume one session in the bundled Copilot runtime with the tools and filters in SessionConfig.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One SDK session operation per create or resume; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same session operation ran with availableTools unset unless an override existed; all runtime tools were therefore eligible except excludedTools.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This remains the terminal expensive boundary for launch. The diff only adds a bounded filter field to its existing payload.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve plugin custom agents and optional prompt overrides before session creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing per-plugin/per-config reads, with ephemeral sessions skipping custom-agent enumeration; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical plugin and prompt-resolution reads occurred before session creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These existing reads can delay launch but remain concurrent where already designed and are not increased by the changed tool filtering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One fixed allow-list of roughly forty built-in names plus two source wildcards per session launch/resume; it does not scale with workspace files, conversation length, or tool invocations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The pre-existing BYOK, shell-tool, and custom-agent work remains joined with Promise.all. The new filter is built once before the single SDK session operation and creates no additional concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The session config is recomputed on cold create and resume; there is no new cache or retry state. The same fixed default is used unless a per-model override replaces it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed launcher line performs only local array construction and passes the result into the pre-existing one-session SDK call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact SDK matching cost is not measured, but it is bounded by a small constant tool list and does not add a boundary call.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The default allow-list adds only bounded launch-time serialization/matching and can prevent future unreviewed built-ins from adding eager prompt work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Submit model turns with tool search enabled or disabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each turn reaches the existing model network request. With tool search active, server definitions marked deferred are omitted from the eager request and may be discovered through the existing tool-search flow when needed; without tool search, all server tools remain eager as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send model requests containing eager tool definitions; when applicable, execute the existing deferred-tool discovery protocol.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At least one model request per turn; additional discovery continuations occur only for deferred tools. The diff does not increase discovery cardinality for the currently wired server-tool set because those definitions already specify deferral explicitly.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Current explicitly deferred tools used the same discovery path and explicitly eager tools stayed eager; unspecified definitions would previously have been eager.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Model requests remain on the turn critical path. The changed fallback can reduce request bytes for future unspecified tools rather than adding an existing product request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward tool-search metadata/results between the runtime and host/client tool implementation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One forwarding sequence per model-requested tool search, with effective candidates deduplicated by tool name; unchanged for current definitions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same bridge handled tools already marked deferLoading true.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only runs when the model searches for a deferred tool and remains an existing continuation on that turn.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Prompt cost scales with model requests and visible tool definitions. The currently wired production server-tool groups explicitly set deferLoading true or false, and per-session exceptions keep set_workspace and active-agent rename eager, so the changed undefined default does not newly defer the current product set.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Model continuations and tool calls retain the runtime's existing sequencing. The diff adds no parallel searches, queue, or burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Tool definitions are fixed at launch and participate in the existing prompt cache. Current materialized tools are refreshed from definitions, preserving their explicit deferral metadata; there is no new retained cache or miss loop.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the current set: repository search and group construction show explicit deferral on all wired production definitions and scoped eager overrides for first-turn tools.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Future contributed server tools that omit deferLoading could trade a discovery continuation for fewer repeated prompt tokens, but no such current hot path is established by the repository definitions.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change establishes a future-safe default without moving a current important tool onto an extra discovery boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run the new built-in allow-list provider integration test in CI
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The test starts one Copilot SDK client, creates four sessions serially (two model profiles with filtered and unfiltered variants), switches each through three modes, reads tool metadata, then stops the client and loopback server.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start and stop one bundled Copilot runtime client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One process lifecycle per test case; introduced by the new test.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This dedicated allow-list test and its runtime process did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds bounded CI test latency only and is required before session metadata can be inspected.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create sessions, set three modes, initialize tools, fetch current metadata, and disconnect.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four sessions; 12 mode changes, 12 initializations, and 12 metadata reads, all serial.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No equivalent allow-list drift probe ran in this test file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These calls define the test's runtime but are constant rather than input-scaled.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serve SDK ancillary requests from a local synthetic endpoint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Bounded by the four session setups and runtime initialization behavior; no external network access.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This test-specific loopback server did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Loopback responses support SDK startup/session creation and do not fan out with repository size.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed at two models, two filter variants, and three modes: four sessions and 36 mode/initialize/metadata RPCs, plus bounded create/disconnect operations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The model and filter loops are serial; one SDK client and one local HTTP server are shared for the single test. There is no unbounded parallel process or request burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A fresh temporary directory and client are used for the test, so this is cold-start work once per test invocation; no state is retained after teardown.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the test loops and process lifecycle establish the exact bounded concurrency and session count.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact CI wall time depends on bundled runtime startup, but all multiplicities are fixed and the test shares one process.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable performance regression. The added CI work is test-only, fixed in cardinality, serial, and directly exercises the runtime behavior under review.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all 16 changed files. Traced session launch/resume, per-turn tool serialization and discovery, runtime tool filtering, and the new integration-test process/RPC boundaries. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue was found, and the PR does not provide enough evidence of a shipped regression fix to record one.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
